Construct a labelled location-and-function map for the seminal vesicles, prostate and Cowper glands. Use the bladder, urethra and prostate as landmarks, and give a different secretion contribution for each gland. Then explain why glandular fluid with no observed sperm does not prove that the glands failed to make sperm. Give two possible upstream or transport explanations.
A human primary spermatocyte has 46 chromosomes just after DNA replication. Which description correctly compares this cell with one product after normal meiosis I?

options.0: The primary cell has two sets and 46 duplicated chromosomes; the product has one set and 23 duplicated chromosomes
options.1: Replication makes the primary cell four sets; meiosis I returns it to two sets
options.2: Meiosis I separates sister chromatids and produces 46 unduplicated chromosomes per product
options.3: The product remains diploid because each chromosome still has two chromatids

activities.title: A model testis has damaged Sertoli cells but functioning interstitial cells. Which pair of direct effects best fits those locations?

options.0: Reduced support for developing sperm; testosterone secretion can remain present
options.1: Reduced testosterone secretion; support for developing sperm remains present
options.2: Reduced seminal-vesicle secretion; sperm support remains present
options.3: Reduced duct contraction; testosterone synthesis shifts to Sertoli cells

activities.title: Which pairing of structure and function is accurate?

options.0: Sertoli cells support developing sperm within seminiferous tubules
options.1: Interstitial cells store mature sperm in the epididymis
options.2: Seminal vesicles produce sperm through meiosis
options.3: The ductus deferens produces testosterone

activities.title: LH and testosterone are within the model range, but developing germ cells show poor survival inside seminiferous tubules. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The pattern points toward impaired Sertoli-cell support or the tubule environment rather than a simple absence of interstitial-cell testosterone production.
options.1: The epididymis is the strongest anatomical location because sperm mature and are stored there after production.
options.2: A ductus deferens obstruction separates successful production from unsuccessful transport and predicts accumulation upstream.
options.3: The observation is enough to prove a single cause, so no comparison or additional evidence is needed.

activities.title: Sperm are present in an epididymis but absent from an ejaculate that still contains accessory-gland fluid. Which additional finding most directly supports a transport obstruction?

options.0: A blocked vas deferens between the epididymis and the urethra
options.1: Reduced germ-cell division within seminiferous tubules
options.2: Reduced testosterone synthesis by interstitial cells
options.3: Reduced fluid secretion by the seminal vesicle

activities.title: Which statement correctly distinguishes an oocyte and its supporting structure?

options.0: An oocyte is the germ cell; a follicle includes the oocyte and surrounding support cells
options.1: A corpus luteum is the ovulated oocyte
options.2: The endometrium produces all ovarian hormones
options.3: Fertilization normally occurs in the cervix

activities.title: A model shows low follicle growth and no dominant follicle before the expected ovulation window. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The strongest first question concerns ovarian follicle development and its hormonal support, before making claims about transport or implantation.
options.1: The uterine tube has a transport role after ovulation and fertilization; an obstruction separates these events from successful arrival in the uterus.
options.2: The pattern directs attention to progesterone signalling or endometrial responsiveness rather than assuming ovulation itself failed.
options.3: The observation is enough to prove a single cause, so no comparison or additional evidence is needed.

activities.title: Ovulation is observed, but a uterine tube is scarred. Which sequence of steps can this structure most directly disrupt?

options.0: Meeting of gametes and movement of the early embryo toward the uterus
options.1: LH release from the pituitary and follicle rupture at the ovary
options.2: Menstrual shedding and milk ejection from the mammary gland
options.3: hCG secretion by the pituitary and sperm production in the tube

activities.title: Which statement best describes sexual development?

options.0: Chromosomes and genes can influence gonads, which can produce hormones whose effects depend on receptors, timing, and target tissues
options.1: A chromosome result directly and completely determines every sex trait and gender
options.2: Testosterone affects every tissue identically
options.3: Every prenatal reproductive hormone is made by the anterior pituitary

activities.title: A fictional karyotype lacks a visible Y chromosome, but an SRY-region test is positive and testicular tissue developed. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: Gene location and expression provide more direct pathway evidence than chromosome appearance alone; the case does not determine identity or every anatomical trait.
options.1: The pattern supports a target-response difference rather than absent hormone production and illustrates why source, signal, receptor, and response must be separated.
options.2: A conversion step can change some androgen-dependent outcomes without implying that all sex traits, fertility, or identity follow one pattern.
options.3: The observation is enough to prove a single cause, so no comparison or additional evidence is needed.

activities.title: In a developmental model, testosterone is produced but androgen receptors on target cells respond poorly. Which step is altered most directly?

options.0: Target-cell response to a hormone already in circulation
options.1: Conversion of the chromosome complement from XY to XX
options.2: Release of every pituitary hormone into circulation
options.3: Movement of chromosomes into the gonadal cells

activities.title: Which hormone-source pairing is correct?

options.0: The hypothalamus releases GnRH, and the anterior pituitary releases FSH and LH
options.1: The pituitary releases testosterone
options.2: The ovaries release GnRH into the uterine tube
options.3: Sertoli cells release LH

activities.title: Repeated measurements in a synthetic testicular model show low testosterone and high LH. Which interpretation best fits the feedback pathway while retaining uncertainty?

options.0: Reduced testosterone feedback can permit more LH release; reduced testicular production or response is one explanation
options.1: High LH demonstrates that the anterior pituitary has stopped releasing hormones
options.2: Low testosterone must suppress LH still further because negative feedback always lowers every hormone
options.3: The two measurements prove that a vas deferens is obstructed

activities.title: A feedback model shows falling testosterone followed by rising LH. Which sequence best explains the LH change?

options.0: Weaker negative feedback permits more hypothalamic/pituitary stimulation
options.1: Stronger negative feedback directly increases pituitary LH release
options.2: Testosterone is converted into LH when its concentration falls
options.3: Sertoli cells release LH to replace missing testosterone

activities.title: Which event is most directly associated with the mid-cycle LH surge in the simplified cycle model?

options.0: Ovulation from a mature follicle
options.1: Immediate implantation in the uterus
options.2: Formation of primary oocytes before birth
options.3: Menstrual shedding caused by rising progesterone

activities.title: Estrogen rises across several model days while progesterone stays low and follicle size increases. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The pattern fits a developing follicular phase and supports proliferative endometrial change before ovulation.
options.1: The temporal sequence supports an ovulatory event in the model, while the graph alone does not establish a real person’s ovulation.
options.2: Declining corpus-luteum support and reduced ovarian hormones explain the transition toward menstruation in the model.
options.3: The observation is enough to prove a single cause, so no comparison or additional evidence is needed.

activities.title: A synthetic cycle records estrogen indices of 5, 10 and 7 on days 7, 12 and 14. LH indices are 3, 6 and 18 on those days. Which interpretation respects both timing and the separate scales?

options.0: The highest sampled estrogen point precedes the highest sampled LH point
options.1: LH concentration on day 14 is 18/7 times the estrogen concentration
options.2: Ovulation must occur exactly two days after the estrogen maximum
options.3: The falling estrogen point marks the end of corpus-luteum function

activities.title: Why can testing matter when a person has no STI symptoms?

options.0: Some infections can be asymptomatic while still being transmissible or affecting tissues
options.1: Every STI immediately produces a unique visible symptom
options.2: Testing can identify the person who transmitted an infection
options.3: A negative symptom check replaces public-health guidance

activities.title: A post states, “No symptoms means no STI, so testing is unnecessary.” Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: Many infections can be asymptomatic; testing decisions should follow current health guidance and individual context rather than symptoms alone.
options.1: Vaccination prevents infection from selected HPV types; it does not treat existing infection and does not protect against unrelated pathogens.
options.2: Some infections can affect reproductive tissues, but causation and current fertility require appropriate clinical evidence and consideration of other factors.
options.3: The observation is enough to prove a single cause, so no comparison or additional evidence is needed.

activities.title: A proposed mechanism links an untreated ascending reproductive-tract infection to impaired fertility. Which intermediate observation best supports that mechanism?

options.0: Inflammation and scarring that reduce patency of the uterine tubes
options.1: More follicles visible in an ovary during the same month
options.2: A larger volume of fluid secreted by an accessory gland
options.3: An intact endometrium measured at one point in the cycle

activities.title: Which statement correctly distinguishes fertilization and implantation?

options.0: Fertilization usually occurs in a uterine tube; implantation is later interaction between a blastocyst and uterine endometrium
options.1: Both events normally occur in the ovary
options.2: Implantation occurs before cleavage begins
options.3: Fertilization is the same event as hCG detection

activities.title: Several small blastomeres remain inside a zona pellucida while the structure is in a uterine tube. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The evidence fits early cleavage during transport; increased cell number has not yet produced a proportional increase in overall size.
options.1: The organized structure fits a blastocyst approaching hatching and implantation rather than an undifferentiated zygote.
options.2: The signal supports trophoblast activity and corpus-luteum maintenance but does not guarantee every later developmental outcome.
options.3: The observation is enough to prove a single cause, so no comparison or additional evidence is needed.

activities.title: After fertilization, an embryo changes from one cell to eight cells with little change in overall size. Which description best accounts for this stage?

options.0: Cleavage partitions the original cytoplasm through mitotic divisions
options.1: Meiosis reduces the chromosome set at each of the three divisions
options.2: Gastrulation forms three germ layers before the second division
options.3: Implantation increases maternal blood flow inside the embryo

activities.title: Which description of placental circulation is accurate?

options.0: Maternal and fetal blood normally remain in separate circulations while substances cross placental tissues
options.1: Maternal and fetal blood normally combine in one shared vessel
options.2: The amnion produces all placental hormones
options.3: The placenta blocks every drug and pathogen

activities.title: Maternal blood arriving near villi has a higher oxygen partial pressure than fetal blood arriving through umbilical arteries. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The gradient and exchange surface support net oxygen movement toward fetal blood without direct blood mixing.
options.1: Facilitated transport and concentration conditions influence glucose transfer; the placenta is not a passive open sieve.
options.2: Molecular size, charge, receptor-mediated routes, and placental biology constrain transfer, so one small-molecule rule cannot be applied to every substance.
options.3: The observation is enough to prove a single cause, so no comparison or additional evidence is needed.

activities.title: In a placental exchange model, oxygen moves from maternal to fetal blood. Which description of the return route is correct?

options.0: The umbilical vein carries blood from the placenta toward the fetus
options.1: The umbilical arteries carry blood from the placenta toward the fetus
options.2: Maternal arteries enter the fetus and become umbilical arteries
options.3: The umbilical vein returns fetal blood from the fetus to the placenta

activities.title: Which germ-layer pairing is accurate?

options.0: Ectoderm contributes to the nervous system, mesoderm to skeletal muscle, and endoderm to much of the digestive epithelial lining
options.1: Ectoderm forms every tissue in the intestine
options.2: Mesoderm forms the epidermis and neural tube
options.3: Endoderm forms all bones and skeletal muscles

activities.title: A developing structure folds from dorsal outer tissue and later forms neurons of the central nervous system. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The evidence supports ectoderm through neural ectoderm and neural-tube development.
options.1: The evidence supports mesodermal origin and illustrates regional differentiation within mesoderm.
options.2: The epithelial lining is primarily endoderm-derived, while surrounding muscle and connective tissues include mesodermal contributions.
options.3: The observation is enough to prove a single cause, so no comparison or additional evidence is needed.

activities.title: A developing intestine includes an epithelial lining and surrounding smooth muscle. Which germ-layer relationship best fits this combination?

options.0: Endoderm contributes the lining; mesoderm contributes the surrounding muscle
options.1: Mesoderm contributes the lining; ectoderm contributes the surrounding muscle
options.2: Ectoderm contributes both tissues because they form one organ
options.3: Endoderm contributes both tissues because the organ encloses a lumen

activities.title: Construct a timeline ordering zygote, blastocyst, gastrulation and early organ formation. In the lesson’s typical two-week-offset example, convert 12 weeks of obstetric gestational age to time since fertilization and identify the developmental period. Give one major developmental pattern in each trimester and explain why the timeline cannot treat organ formation as the end of maturation.
A synthetic model shows a tissue-specific effect only when exposure overlaps that tissue’s early differentiation window. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The timing-mechanism match strengthens a developmental explanation, while dose and applicability to humans still require evidence.
options.1: The association warrants investigation, but confounding prevents a claim that the exposure alone caused the entire difference.
options.2: Converging dose-response and mechanism evidence strengthens causal inference without making every individual outcome predictable.
options.3: The observation is enough to prove a single cause, so no comparison or additional evidence is needed.

activities.title: In a synthetic cell model, marker M occurs in 4/40 controls and 20/40 exposed early-stage samples, versus 5/40 controls and 9/40 exposed later-stage samples. Which comparison best tests whether the exposure effect depends on stage?

options.0: Compare the early difference of 0.40 with the later difference of 0.10
options.1: Compare the exposed counts 20 and 9 while omitting both controls
options.2: Combine all exposed and control samples before examining stage
options.3: Compare 20/4 with 9/5 and report both as probabilities

activities.title: Which pairing is accurate in the simplified lactation model?

options.0: Prolactin supports milk production, while oxytocin supports milk ejection
options.1: Oxytocin produces all milk nutrients
options.2: Prolactin directly causes cervical dilation during labour
options.3: Milk production and ejection are the same target response

activities.title: Cervical stretch increases, oxytocin release rises, and uterine contractions strengthen until delivery. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: This is a positive-feedback loop because the response increases the initiating stretch until an endpoint removes the stimulus.
options.1: The pathway emphasizes prolactin action on production and depends on repeated neural-endocrine signalling over time.
options.2: The pathway describes a neuroendocrine ejection reflex, distinct from the slower synthesis of milk.
options.3: The observation is enough to prove a single cause, so no comparison or additional evidence is needed.

activities.title: Which change most directly interrupts the cervical-stretch feedback loop after delivery?

options.0: Removal of the fetus reduces the stretch stimulus that supported the loop
options.1: Oxytocin is converted to prolactin after the final contraction
options.2: Cervical stretch starts inhibiting every uterine contraction
options.3: The placenta becomes the main source of pituitary oxytocin

activities.title: What is the most important first step when comparing reproductive technologies?

options.0: Identify the reproductive process each technology changes and the outcome its evidence actually measures
options.1: Assume the highest percentage uses the same denominator
options.2: Treat pregnancy prevention and STI prevention as identical
options.3: Choose solely from the technology name

activities.title: A device physically reduces sperm movement and is evaluated by pregnancy rate over one year of use. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The mechanism is mechanical and the outcome needs a defined use context; STI protection must be evaluated separately for the specific barrier and infection.
options.1: The reported denominator omits earlier cycle attrition, so a decision brief should also examine outcomes per initiated cycle and the relevant population.
options.2: The technology repairs one transport step; later conception and development remain probabilistic and depend on additional factors.
options.3: The observation is enough to prove a single cause, so no comparison or additional evidence is needed.

activities.title: A fictional service reports 30 live births from 60 embryo transfers. Those transfers came from 100 initiated IVF cycles. What are the live-birth percentages per transfer and per initiated cycle?

options.0: 50% per transfer; 30% per initiated cycle
options.1: 30% per transfer; 50% per initiated cycle
options.2: 60% per transfer; 30% per initiated cycle
options.3: 50% per transfer; 60% per initiated cycle

activities.title: Two fictional models have different problems. Model A has low upstream hormone support, responsive target tissue and an open passage. Model B has working gamete production and signals but a blocked passage. Predict how hormone support or restoring the passage could address each model’s cause. State a condition for each prediction and explain why success at that step would not guarantee a live birth. Evaluate mechanisms only; do not recommend a treatment.

Gonadotropin and gonadal-hormone patterns fit the model range, gamete-production evidence is present, and one transport pathway is obstructed. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The converging evidence supports a localized transport explanation before an endocrine one; pathway imaging or patency evidence would further discriminate.
options.1: Reduced upstream stimulation is more consistent than an isolated gonadal or transport failure, though timing and repeated measurements remain important.
options.2: The mechanism may be appropriate, but the statistic omits earlier attrition; outcomes per initiated cycle and matched-population evidence are needed.
options.3: The observation is enough to prove a single cause, so no comparison or additional evidence is needed.

activities.title: An isolated-cell experiment finds that added LH increases testosterone when interstitial cells are present, but not when they are removed. Which next comparison most directly tests the role of those cells?

options.0: Restore interstitial cells and compare testosterone with a matched no-LH condition
options.1: Count sperm in a duct while changing both temperature and hormone dose
options.2: Measure accessory-gland fluid without recording interstitial-cell presence
options.3: Replace testosterone measurements with total cell count in both groups

activities.title: In a fictional model, germ cells are present and testosterone release continues, but the vas deferens is blocked. Trace the route from sperm production to delivery and identify the first disrupted step.
A human primary spermatocyte has replicated its DNA. State chromosome number and duplication at the start, after meiosis I and after meiosis II. Add one distinct hormonal support pathway.
Draw or write a labelled route linking ovulation, usual fertilization site and implantation. Distinguish the oocyte from the follicle and name its usual meiotic state at ovulation.

Construct four separate hormone graphs from the supplied six-day table. Choose labelled axes and an appropriate scale, then enter every point. Explain the estrogen–LH sequence and the later progesterone change. State one limitation of sparse, separately scaled indices.
Order fertilization, cleavage, morula, blastocyst and implantation. Explain how chromosome number and overall size differ during the early cleavage sequence.
Connect trophoblast, hCG, corpus luteum and progesterone in an early-pregnancy pathway. Then give one derivative of each germ layer without treating hCG as a germ layer.
Trace oxygen from the maternal side of the placenta into fetal circulation. Name the umbilical vessels by direction and explain why an exchange diagram must keep the two blood supplies distinct.
Write one positive-feedback loop in labour and distinguish the two main hormonal roles in lactation. State an endpoint or physiological qualification.
Place germ cells, Sertoli cells and interstitial cells in the correct tissue locations. Compare an open-duct production defect with a blocked-duct case.
Compare cytoplasm and chromosome outcomes of one primary spermatocyte and one primary oocyte in the usual human model.
Construct a feedback diagram for sustained high estrogen before ovulation and falling progesterone late in a non-pregnant cycle.
Explain what success per embryo transfer excludes when a clinic reports an IVF percentage.
Build a three-layer tissue map including nervous tissue, epidermis, muscle, skeleton, digestive lining and respiratory lining.
Compare a barrier, a hormonal method and surgical duct interruption by altered step, evidence needed and one separate decision criterion.

Using the supplied fictional cases, state a testable prediction that distinguishes a production problem from a transport obstruction. Compare at least two tissue, signal or passage observations. Design a repeated comparison, naming conditions to keep consistent. A reviewer claims, “Every low-delivery result means sperm production failed.” Respond to this claim, give another possible explanation, and revise the conclusion. Name a further observation that would distinguish the explanations.

Use the synthetic hormone series to state a testable prediction about estrogen, LH and later progesterone order. Report at least two named values with days and retain their separate relative scales. Design a repeated comparison with consistent sampling conditions. A reviewer claims, “The LH peak proves ovulation occurred exactly on day 14.” Respond with an alternative, revise the claim, and name an independent observation that could test ovulation.

Use the supplied non-human cell-model counts to test whether the exposure contrast differs by stage. Calculate both exposed-minus-control proportions and state a testable prediction for repeated trials. Design a comparison with controlled dose, duration and culture conditions. A reviewer claims, “These percentages give the exact risk to a human embryo.” Respond with an alternative explanation, revise the claim, and name evidence that would strengthen the stage-dependent model interpretation.

A primary spermatocyte begins meiosis with 46 duplicated chromosomes. One homologous pair fails to separate in meiosis I; meiosis II then separates sisters normally. Predict chromosome counts in the four products and identify the observation that would distinguish this from a meiosis-II error.

A sparse cycle record shows rising estrogen followed by an LH peak. A learner concludes that ovulation definitely occurred. If the follicle did not rupture, which conclusion fails? Name a later observation that would help test ovulation and explain why hormone timing alone is insufficient.

A placenta model initially keeps oxygen gradient, exchange area and barrier thickness constant. Now reduce only exchange area. Predict the direction of the change in oxygen transfer, retain the correct umbilical vessel directions, and name a comparison that tests the prediction.

In a lactation model, prolactin signalling remains active but oxytocin signalling is blocked. Predict which immediate process is most directly impaired. Propose an observation that distinguishes reduced milk ejection from reduced milk synthesis.

A fictional reproductive-health information project must choose between the two formats in the table. Compare all five perspective rows, then make an initial choice. A participant now explains that internet access at home is unreliable and a shared device cannot be used privately. Revise your choice or justify retaining it with a specific adaptation. Explain one way hormone research changed technological capability and one way a societal need shaped that research. Keep programme preferences separate from biological evidence; neither format establishes the suitability of a treatment for an individual.

A fictional information service reports 12 live births, 30 embryo transfers and 50 initiated cycles. It proposes a short headline, “40% success”, to meet demand for understandable information. Calculate both live-birth percentages and repair the headline. Explain how IVF can expand capability for a transport problem without guaranteeing later development. Use the five requests in the table to compare the short headline with a fuller explanation. After considering the budget objection, revise the communication plan or justify retaining it. Do not recommend a treatment or rank family forms.
